quote: Hermes is MIT-licensed, model-agnostic and self-hosted, reachable through Telegram, Slack, WhatsApp, Signal or email, with persistent memory, self-written skills and a built-in scheduler. It is excellent, and it gave me the same magical feeling I had when I first set up OpenClaw. But it's definitely also a developer's tool, and most knowledge workers will find the setup intimidating.
author: Christian Pean
notes: Surgeon: Hermes excellent/OpenClaw-magic feel but developer-tool setup barrier.

quote: Running Opus 5.5 with a 1M window through a Claude subscription plugin in Hermes Agent burned the limit by lunch, because every turn re-read about 800K tokens of old chat. The fix: compress early and per model.
author: Clauday
notes: Sep 27 Clauday: Hermes+Claude 1M re-read ~800K tokens/turn, burned limit by lunch.

quote: Raft is a Slack where humans and AI agents clock in together, and the team open-sourced the whole thing: server, web, CLI, the agent daemon and desktop app. Each agent has a name, role and memory stored locally; they claim tasks, hand off and review each other. Claude Code, Codex and Hermes can join a channel on your own subscription.
author: Clauday
notes: Sep 27 Clauday: Raft open-source Slack-with-agents; Hermes can join.

quote: A solo founder says they are officially off the terminal and local development: a Claude-native workflow now hands back completed tasks backed by full end-to-end QA and verification. They tried the same idea early in the year with OpenClaw and Hermes and found it hacky; now it runs across code, design, marketing and support from anywhere.
author: Clauday
notes: Sep 28 Clauday: early OpenClaw/Hermes hacky vs Claude-native now.
